entries.name: expectTypeOf
notes: WARNINGDuring runtime this function doesn't do anything. To enable typechecking, don't forget to pass down --typecheck flag.

children.name: not
children.description: You can negate all assertions, using .not property.

children.name: toEqualTypeOf
children.description: This matcher will check if the types are fully equal to each other. This matcher will not fail if two objects have different values, but the same type. It will fail however if an object is missing a property.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf({ a: 1 }).toEqualTypeOf<{ a: number }>()
expectTypeOf({ a: 1 }).toEqualTypeOf({ a: 1 })
expectTypeOf({ a: 1 }).toEqualTypeOf({ a: 2 })
expectTypeOf({ a: 1, b: 1 }).not.toEqualTypeOf<{ a: number }>()

children.name: toMatchTypeOf
children.description: This matcher checks if expect type extends provided type. It is different from toEqual and is more similar to expect's toMatchObject(). With this matcher, you can check if an object “matches” a type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf({ a: 1, b: 1 }).toMatchTypeOf({ a: 1 })
expectTypeOf<number>().toMatchTypeOf<string | number>()
expectTypeOf<string | number>().not.toMatchTypeOf<number>()

notes: DEPRECATEDThis matcher has been deprecated since expect-type v1.2.0. Use toExtend instead.

children.name: toExtend
children.description: This matcher checks if expect type extends provided type. It is different from toEqual and is more similar to expect's toMatchObject(). With this matcher, you can check if an object "matches" a type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf({ a: 1, b: 1 }).toExtend({ a: 1 })
expectTypeOf<number>().toExtend<string | number>()
expectTypeOf<string | number>().not.toExtend<number>()

children.name: toMatchObjectType
children.description: This matcher performs a strict check on object types, ensuring that the expected type matches the provided object type. It's stricter than toExtend and is the recommended choice when working with object types as it's more likely to catch issues like readonly properties.
notes: WARNINGThis matcher only works with plain object types. It will fail for union types and other complex types. For those cases, use toExtend instead.

children.name: extract
children.description: You can use .extract to narrow down types for further testing.
notes: WARNINGIf no type is found in the union, .extract will return never.

children.name: exclude
children.description: You can use .exclude to remove types from a union for further testing.
notes: WARNINGIf no type is found in the union, .exclude will return never.

children.name: returns
children.description: You can use .returns to extract return value of a function type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(() => {}).returns.toBeVoid()
expectTypeOf((a: number) => [a, a]).returns.toEqualTypeOf([1, 2])

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: parameters
children.description: You can extract function arguments with .parameters to perform assertions on its value. Parameters are returned as an array.
signatures:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

type NoParam = () => void
type HasParam = (s: string) => void

expectTypeOf<NoParam>().parameters.toEqualTypeOf<[]>()
expectTypeOf<HasParam>().parameters.toEqualTypeOf<[string]>()

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

type NoParam = () => void
type HasParam = (s: string) => void

expectTypeOf<NoParam>().parameters.toEqualTypeOf<[]>()
expectTypeOf<HasParam>().parameters.toEqualTypeOf<[string]>()

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.
TIPYou can also use .toBeCallableWith matcher as a more expressive assertion.

children.name: parameter
children.description: You can extract a certain function argument with .parameter(number) call to perform other assertions on it.
notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: constructorParameters
children.description: You can extract constructor parameters as an array of values and perform assertions on them with this method.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(Date).constructorParameters.toEqualTypeOf<[] | [string | number | Date]>()

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.
TIPYou can also use .toBeConstructibleWith matcher as a more expressive assertion.

children.name: instance
children.description: This property gives access to matchers that can be performed on an instance of the provided class.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(Date).instance.toHaveProperty('toISOString')

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: items
children.description: You can get array item type with .items to perform further assertions.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf([1, 2, 3]).items.toEqualTypeOf<number>()
expectTypeOf([1, 2, 3]).items.not.toEqualTypeOf<string>()

children.name: resolves
children.description: This matcher extracts resolved value of a Promise, so you can perform other assertions on it.
notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-promise type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: guards
children.description: This matcher extracts guard value (e.g., v is number), so you can perform assertions on it.
notes: WARNINGReturns never, if the value is not a guard function, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: asserts
children.description: This matcher extracts assert value (e.g., assert v is number), so you can perform assertions on it.
notes: WARNINGReturns never, if the value is not an assert function, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: toBeAny
children.description: With this matcher you can check, if provided type is any type. If the type is too specific, the test will fail.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf<any>().toBeAny()
expectTypeOf({} as any).toBeAny()
expectTypeOf('string').not.toBeAny()

children.name: toBeUnknown
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is unknown type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf().toBeUnknown()
expectTypeOf({} as unknown).toBeUnknown()
expectTypeOf('string').not.toBeUnknown()

children.name: toBeNever
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is a never type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf<never>().toBeNever()
expectTypeOf((): never => {}).returns.toBeNever()

children.name: toBeFunction
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is a function.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(42).not.toBeFunction()
expectTypeOf((): never => {}).toBeFunction()

children.name: toBeObject
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is an object.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(42).not.toBeObject()
expectTypeOf({}).toBeObject()

children.name: toBeArray
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is Array<T>.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(42).not.toBeArray()
expectTypeOf([]).toBeArray()
expectTypeOf([1, 2]).toBeArray()
expectTypeOf([{}, 42]).toBeArray()

children.name: toBeString
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is a string.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(42).not.toBeString()
expectTypeOf('').toBeString()
expectTypeOf('a').toBeString()

children.name: toBeBoolean
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is boolean.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(42).not.toBeBoolean()
expectTypeOf(true).toBeBoolean()
expectTypeOf<boolean>().toBeBoolean()

children.name: toBeVoid
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is void.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(() => {}).returns.toBeVoid()
expectTypeOf<void>().toBeVoid()

children.name: toBeSymbol
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is a symbol.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(Symbol(1)).toBeSymbol()
expectTypeOf<symbol>().toBeSymbol()

children.name: toBeNull
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is null.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(null).toBeNull()
expectTypeOf<null>().toBeNull()
expectTypeOf(undefined).not.toBeNull()

children.name: toBeUndefined
children.description: This matcher checks, if provided type is undefined.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(undefined).toBeUndefined()
expectTypeOf<undefined>().toBeUndefined()
expectTypeOf(null).not.toBeUndefined()

children.name: toBeNullable
children.description: This matcher checks, if you can use null or undefined with provided type.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf<undefined | 1>().toBeNullable()
expectTypeOf<null | 1>().toBeNullable()
expectTypeOf<undefined | null | 1>().toBeNullable()

children.name: toBeCallableWith
children.description: This matcher ensures you can call provided function with a set of parameters.
signatures:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

type NoParam = () => void
type HasParam = (s: string) => void

expectTypeOf<NoParam>().toBeCallableWith()
expectTypeOf<HasParam>().toBeCallableWith('some string')

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

type NoParam = () => void
type HasParam = (s: string) => void

expectTypeOf<NoParam>().toBeCallableWith()
expectTypeOf<HasParam>().toBeCallableWith('some string')

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: toBeConstructibleWith
children.description: This matcher ensures you can create a new instance with a set of constructor parameters.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

expectTypeOf(Date).toBeConstructibleWith(new Date())
expectTypeOf(Date).toBeConstructibleWith('01-01-2000')

notes: WARNINGIf used on a non-function type, it will return never, so you won't be able to chain it with other matchers.

children.name: toHaveProperty
children.description: This matcher checks if a property exists on the provided object. If it exists, it also returns the same set of matchers for the type of this property, so you can chain assertions one after another.

examples.code:
import { expectTypeOf } from 'vitest'

const obj = { a: 1, b: '' }

expectTypeOf(obj).toHaveProperty('a')
expectTypeOf(obj).not.toHaveProperty('c')

expectTypeOf(obj).toHaveProperty('a').toBeNumber()
expectTypeOf(obj).toHaveProperty('b').toBeString()
expectTypeOf(obj).toHaveProperty('a').not.toBeString()

notes: Type: <K extends keyof T>(property: K) => ExpectTypeOf<T[K>

children.name: branded
children.description: You can use .branded to allow type assertions to succeed for types that are semantically equivalent but differ in representation.
notes: WARNINGThis helper comes at a performance cost and can cause the TypeScript compiler to 'give up' if used with excessively deep types. Use it sparingly and only when necessary.
